internal_tensions.NAME: Continuity versus authorised correction
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Adjudicate the actual supported obligation and oracle warrant; characterisation is evidence, not automatic veto.

ACCOUNT.VALUES: Continuity of relied-on behaviour versus necessary correction/adaptation.
ACCOUNT.COSTS: Preserving faults harms users; breaking relied-on behaviour creates transition cost.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: A legitimate supported consumer relies on the behaviour and no authorised revision exists.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: The behaviour violates the accepted objective or an authorised new obligation, with consequences addressed.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Compatibility window or explicit old/new mode with tested semantics and support horizon.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Two ambiguous meanings, unmaintained compatibility mode, or an oracle changed solely to pass.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Identify the actual obligation, consumer and authorisation for revision; unresolved authority blocks that revision, not unrelated work.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Existing usage does not itself establish legitimacy; disagreement can persist.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Continuity versus necessary behavioural change

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Preserve relied-on behaviour and downstream trust.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Correct defects and obsolete requirements.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Preserve behaviour with a current supported consumer; change it when legitimate intent is revised and transition consequences are addressed. A failing characterisation test is a question, not automatic veto.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Separate preservation and changed obligations within one patch when needed.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: A compatibility layer can retain the defect indefinitely while the new path creates incompatible semantics.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Unknown consumers can prevent confident removal.

COSTS.A: Preservation retains defects or obsolete constraints and can burden migration.
COSTS.B: Behavioural change can break legitimate dependencies and trust.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Supported current consumers rely on the behaviour.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Current legitimate intent requires a different outcome.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Test preservation versus correction of obsolete behaviour

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Existing outputs provide evidence about undocumented use.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: New intent can legitimately invalidate old outputs.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Adjudicate the supported observer and oracle provenance. Gold-patch identity alone cannot settle correctness.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Keep unaffected characterisation while replacing explicitly obsolete assertions with independently justified expectations.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Updating all golden files automatically makes the patch its own oracle.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Historical intent may be unrecoverable.

COSTS.A: Preserving snapshots can institutionalise a defect.
COSTS.B: Revising expectations can erase evidence of a relied-on behaviour.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: The observed result has a current justified consumer or contract.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Independent intent or evidence establishes the old result should change.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.VALUES: Continuity of relied-on behaviour versus necessary correction/adaptation.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS: Preserving faults harms users; breaking relied-on behaviour creates transition cost.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.FAVOURS_FIRST: A legitimate supported consumer relies on the behaviour and no authorised revision exists.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.FAVOURS_SECOND: The behaviour violates the accepted objective or an authorised new obligation, with consequences addressed.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Compatibility window or explicit old/new mode with tested semantics and support horizon.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.HYBRID_FAILURE: Two ambiguous meanings, unmaintained compatibility mode, or an oracle changed solely to pass.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.DISCRIMINATOR: Identify the actual obligation, consumer and authorisation for revision; unresolved authority blocks that revision, not unrelated work.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.UNCERTAINTY: Existing usage does not itself establish legitimacy; disagreement can persist.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TITLE: Continuity versus necessary behavioural change

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Preserve relied-on behaviour and downstream trust.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Correct defects and obsolete requirements.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.DISCRIMINATOR: Preserve behaviour with a current supported consumer; change it when legitimate intent is revised and transition consequences are addressed. A failing characterisation test is a question, not automatic veto.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Separate preservation and changed obligations within one patch when needed.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.HYBRID_FAILURE: A compatibility layer can retain the defect indefinitely while the new path creates incompatible semantics.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.UNCERTAINTY: Unknown consumers can prevent confident removal.

COSTS.A: Preservation retains defects or obsolete constraints and can burden migration.
COSTS.B: Behavioural change can break legitimate dependencies and trust.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Supported current consumers rely on the behaviour.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Current legitimate intent requires a different outcome.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TITLE: Test preservation versus correction of obsolete behaviour

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Existing outputs provide evidence about undocumented use.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: New intent can legitimately invalidate old outputs.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.DISCRIMINATOR: Adjudicate the supported observer and oracle provenance. Gold-patch identity alone cannot settle correctness.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Keep unaffected characterisation while replacing explicitly obsolete assertions with independently justified expectations.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.HYBRID_FAILURE: Updating all golden files automatically makes the patch its own oracle.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.UNCERTAINTY: Historical intent may be unrecoverable.

COSTS.A: Preserving snapshots can institutionalise a defect.
COSTS.B: Revising expectations can erase evidence of a relied-on behaviour.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: The observed result has a current justified consumer or contract.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Independent intent or evidence establishes the old result should change.

internal_tensions.NAME: Familiarity versus task-beneficial simplification
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Compare future task capability with relearning, review and regression cost.

ACCOUNT.VALUES: Familiarity and domain knowledge versus simplification of costly structure.
ACCOUNT.COSTS: Change can destroy valuable tacit knowledge; non-change can retain avoidable complexity.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: Few expected changes, scarce expertise and useful stable behaviour.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: Repeated task-specific cost and credible ability to transfer knowledge.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Small verified transformations with retained rationale and representative maintenance tasks.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Long-lived mixed styles and half-transferred knowledge make both old and new harder to understand.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Compare demonstrated next-change capability and total transition cost, not complexity score alone.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Future demand and learning cost remain uncertain.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Familiarity versus simplification

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Known structure reduces learning and operational uncertainty.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Better task structure may reduce recurring burden.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Prefer restructuring when a plausible recurrent task benefit exceeds relearning, review and regression cost; prefer familiarity when the system is stable or retiring.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Small seam extraction with local learning and task evaluation.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Partial abstraction adds indirection without retiring old concepts, making both models necessary.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Long-term benefit is confounded by concurrent work.

COSTS.A: Familiar structure can retain expensive recurrent work.
COSTS.B: Simplification incurs relearning, review and regression risk.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Stable use, short remaining life or weak evidence of recurrent difficulty.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Credible repeated future tasks benefit enough to offset transition.

internal_tensions.NAME: Local repair versus structural replacement
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Use unmet obligations, feasible support, seams and prospective transition cost rather than age or sunk effort.

ACCOUNT.COSTS: A cheap patch may compound systemic cost; replacement can lose hidden requirements and create dual support.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: Bounded impact, adequate support and a short or stable horizon.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: Required capability cannot be supported economically by available local changes.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Incremental transfer over validated seams with explicit exit.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Permanent adapters and dual data authorities add migration cost without eliminating legacy cost.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Compare feasible obligations, seam/data constraints and prospective costs including the exit, not sunk effort.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Published migration accounts rarely establish representative comparative rates.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Local repair versus replacement

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Retain embedded domain knowledge and avoid transition risk.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Remove constraints that bounded repair cannot economically address.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Choose by unmet obligations, support feasibility and lifecycle cost including transition; age alone has no deciding role.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Incremental displacement at a real functional/data boundary.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: A wrapper freezes obsolete constraints while adding a second maintenance burden.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Few unbiased controlled whole-migration comparisons exist.

COSTS.A: Repair can perpetuate an unserviceable foundation.
COSTS.B: Replacement incurs knowledge recovery, conversion and transition risk.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Bounded unmet need and viable support for the existing foundation.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Core obligations cannot be met economically by bounded maintenance.

internal_tensions.NAME: Automation throughput versus total review burden
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Compare accepted outcomes and full version-specific work; correct and deceptive suggestions differ.

ACCOUNT.VALUES: Automation throughput versus validation, comprehension and review burden.
ACCOUNT.COSTS: Human work may move rather than disappear; refusing suitable automation also has opportunity cost.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: A bounded task class with aligned oracles and observed end-to-end benefit.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: Ambiguous requirements, unstable tools, poor harness or expensive review.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Scoped generation with selective independent checks and outcome feedback.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Several tools share one invalid oracle, or the human rubber-stamps unreviewable volume.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Compare accepted outcomes and total work, including later repair, on representative tasks under versioned settings.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: ESME-088 remains unresolved; contemporary follow-up does not establish a universal speedup.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Automated transformation versus review burden

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Generate useful candidates and reduce repetitive work.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Avoid deceptive patches, hidden validation work and unauthorised action.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Evaluate correct outcomes and full cost for the task and tool version. Strong narrow transformations can need less manual review; weak oracles demand more independent evidence.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Bounded generator plus targeted independent checks and authorised acceptance.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Reviewer time rises while approval becomes perfunctory, producing neither speed nor reliable correction.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Current population-wide effect remains uncertain.

COSTS.A: Manual inspection has attention and latency costs.
COSTS.B: Generation and review can increase total work and confidence in wrong patches.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Weak oracles, open-ended intent or unsupported task transfer.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: A supported bounded transformation with useful independent checks.

internal_tensions.NAME: Fast feedback versus evidence breadth
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Retain critical pending checks and representative loss-bearing observations; early green is not complete.

ACCOUNT.VALUES: Fast feedback/release versus breadth and representativeness of evidence.
ACCOUNT.COSTS: Broad tests delay useful repairs; narrow selection and short canaries miss consequential cases.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: Cheap reversible effects and reliable scoped dependency/sampling assumptions.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: High loss, unknown dependencies, rare effects or shared state.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Early prioritised feedback plus explicit completion criteria and targeted broader validation.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Early green results become unspoken permission to omit the only test for a live obligation.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Identify the loss-bearing observation and whether the chosen method can actually detect it before unacceptable exposure.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: No universal acceptable test coverage or canary duration follows.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Early feedback versus evidence breadth

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Expose actionable failures before expensive commitment.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Avoid skipping rare but important checks.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: A release decision may wait for critical checks even when routine feedback is prioritised. Small suites favour retest-all.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Run quick discriminating checks early and retain explicit pending obligations.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Skipped work is labelled passed, so latency improvement is purchased with false assurance.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Rare delayed failures can dominate otherwise favourable averages.

COSTS.A: Broader evidence delays feedback and consumes execution resources.
COSTS.B: Selection and priority can miss or delay consequential failures.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Critical consequences require broad checks before action.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Ordering changes a useful action and selection assumptions hold.

internal_tensions.NAME: Debt reduction versus current useful delivery
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Use contingent recurrence/horizon and explicit opportunity cost; avoid both endless cleanup and permanent deferral excuses.

ACCOUNT.VALUES: Debt reduction versus current useful delivery.
ACCOUNT.COSTS: Repayment consumes present resources and can regress; deferral can block or multiply later work.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: Credible repeated interest or a near-term required change whose cost is reduced.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: Low future use, inexpensive interest, impending retirement or more urgent obligations.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Bounded structural improvement during relevant work with an explicit opportunity-cost account.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Endless incidental cleanup hides scope expansion; feature urgency becomes a permanent excuse to ignore a known liability.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: State the change-contingent cost mechanism, horizon and uncertainty that could reverse priority.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Precise economic calibration is not generally established.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Debt reduction versus current value

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Avoid recurring maintenance burden and future loss of options.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Deliver urgent user value and conserve finite capacity.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Prioritise expected consequential burden within a plausible horizon; stop when retirement or changed demand removes prospective benefit.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Bounded remediation alongside a necessary change when coupling is genuine.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Opportunistic cleanup enlarges a critical fix until both value and debt work are delayed.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Future change frequency and shifted costs are uncertain.

COSTS.A: Immediate value work may leave compounding future burdens.
COSTS.B: Debt work can defer urgent user value and never reach payback.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Urgent obligations, short horizon or uncertain interest.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: A plausible repeated burden has a supported horizon and affected consumer.

internal_tensions.NAME: Downstream continuity versus finite support capacity
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Use real supported promises, willing capacity and feasible transition; popularity creates neither infinite duty nor permission to abandon.

ACCOUNT.VALUES: Downstream continuity versus finite support capacity and upstream freedom to evolve.
ACCOUNT.COSTS: Unlimited compatibility can exhaust maintainers; abrupt discontinuity can strand dependent users.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_FIRST: Live accepted support commitments and high consumer migration costs.
ACCOUNT.FAVOURS_SECOND: Unfunded/expired commitments, unsafe unsupported dependencies or viable consumer alternatives.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Explicit support windows, actionable deprecation and scoped version variants.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Dates are announced without a viable path, or compatibility branches multiply beyond capacity.
ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Determine real promises, capacity and transition feasibility; usage popularity is neither permission nor an infinite support contract.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Unknown consumers and disputed responsibilities remain possible.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Continuity versus responsible ending

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Support users and preserve knowledge.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: End unsustainable labour and unnecessary live operation.

ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: A nominal handoff names an unwilling owner while the old team still supplies unpaid support.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Unknown consumers and unfunded obligations resist tidy closure.

COSTS.A: Continued support consumes scarce labour and may prolong obsolete risk.
COSTS.B: Ending service can impose transition costs and remove useful access.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Current obligations and willing capable support remain.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Continued operation lacks justified value or feasible support and obligations can be resolved.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TITLE: Continuity versus responsible ending

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Support users and preserve knowledge.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: End unsustainable labour and unnecessary live operation.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.DISCRIMINATOR: Retain service only for justified obligations with feasible capacity; archives can meet historical needs without a running service.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Time-bounded transition and retained source/history with clear limits.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.HYBRID_FAILURE: A nominal handoff names an unwilling owner while the old team still supplies unpaid support.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.UNCERTAINTY: Unknown consumers and unfunded obligations resist tidy closure.

COSTS.A: Continued support consumes scarce labour and may prolong obsolete risk.
COSTS.B: Ending service can impose transition costs and remove useful access.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Current obligations and willing capable support remain.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Continued operation lacks justified value or feasible support and obligations can be resolved.

internal_tensions.NAME: Coexistence versus quiescent cutover
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Choose by partitionability, reconciliation cost and a credible accepted interruption; incoherent hybrids can incur both burdens.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Coexistence versus quiescent cutover

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Avoid a concentrated outage and obtain incremental learning.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Avoid dual-state, gateway and mixed-version complexity.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Use coexistence only when partition and reconciliation costs are tolerable; use quiescence when an accepted stable boundary is credible.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Read-only or bounded-phase coexistence with explicit data authority.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Dual writes without authority create divergence while neither system can be retired.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: External concurrent writers can defeat the planned boundary.

COSTS.A: Coexistence creates gateways, data authority and dual-support costs.
COSTS.B: Quiescence concentrates interruption and cutover risk.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Useful partition, tolerable reconciliation and costly interruption.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: An accepted stable write boundary and expensive or infeasible coexistence.

internal_tensions.NAME: Impact confidence versus investigation cost
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Scale challenge to plausible missed-effect consequence; correlated tool agreement does not justify unbounded analysis.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Impact completeness versus investigation cost

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Find consequential downstream effects.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Avoid false-positive work and whole-system paralysis.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Scale challenge effort to plausible missed-edge consequence and evidence quality; accept demonstrably local changes locally.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Typed impact hypothesis with selective independent challenges.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: Combining several correlated tools produces a huge impact set without improving recall of real hidden effects.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: Rare unknown dependencies remain difficult to price.

COSTS.A: Broad analysis consumes time and produces false positives.
COSTS.B: Local inquiry can miss a high-consequence dependency.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: Uncertain edges or high missed-effect consequence.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: A supported small boundary and affordable counterexample challenge.

internal_tensions.NAME: Learning versus stable, non-circular acceptance rules
internal_tensions.DISCRIMINATOR: Revise on a bounded hypothesis with independent warrant or separately authorised new intent; keep or retire methods when appropriate.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Learning versus stable acceptance rules

PROTECTED_VALUES.A: Revise failing or overly costly maintenance methods.
PROTECTED_VALUES.B: Prevent a successor from validating itself by weakening obligations.

ACCOUNT.DISCRIMINATOR: Changes to method need external authority and evidence tied to a real failure or cost; unchanged methods and control removal remain options.
ACCOUNT.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Bounded trial evaluated against predecessor obligations or separately authorised new intent.
ACCOUNT.HYBRID_FAILURE: A meta-process consumes more attention than it saves and endlessly revises its own success measures.
ACCOUNT.UNCERTAINTY: The integrated revision mechanism has not been empirically validated as a system.

COSTS.A: Stable rules may preserve a failing or unnecessarily costly method.
COSTS.B: Frequent revision destabilises acceptance and adds meta-work.

CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.A: The existing method is effective with no consequential new evidence.
CONTEXTS_FAVOURING_EACH.B: Observed failure, changed constraints or demonstrated avoidable cost.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CASE: Refactor passes tests but changes an external observer
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.SETUP: A structural transformation preserves usual return values but changes reflection, serialization, binary layout or an API client’s required behaviour.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.EXPECTED_DECISION: Reject the unqualified preservation claim; widen the observer or authorise an actual behaviour/compatibility change.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NON_TRIGGER: The excluded observation is outside supported use and no legitimate consumer relies on it.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.FALSIFIER_OR_FAILURE: Testing only the original input/output model can give false assurance even if the transformation rule is sound within that model.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Analytical scenario uses published observer/tool limitations; not a measured rate of refactoring failure.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TITLE: Refactor passes tests but changes an external observer

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.SETUP: A justified new supported configuration adds branching or modules and increases a complexity score.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Shared objective and meaningful category comparisons, not one checked box.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Requester, planner, maintainer

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Classify the purposes of a change using stated definitions, permit multiple purposes and explain disagreement where the distinction changes a decision. Failure: Single labels obscure mixed motives, confuse restoring intent with revising it, and distort effort accounts.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Maintainers and planning consumers agree operational definitions; a classifier has no authority to approve the underlying change.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: A common unit of classification and enough request context to distinguish intent, environment and prevention.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Use ordinary language when no decision depends on a taxonomy; do not force every commit into one exclusive category.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: Classification informs planning, funding, reporting or selection of preservation obligations.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Ordinary language loses aggregate comparability; accept that loss when no credible allocation or planning decision uses the categories.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: State the requested behavioural difference, surviving obligations and decision authority; challenge ambiguous or conflicting requests before treating tests as acceptance. Failure: A technically valid patch can solve the wrong problem or preserve an obligation that its legitimate owner has withdrawn.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Request owner and affected obligation holders determine the objective; implementers can question feasibility but cannot silently redefine acceptance.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: An identifiable baseline, affected interests and an actor entitled to resolve the objective; emergency delegation must be explicit.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Use an existing unambiguous authorised request; no new board or document is needed. Decline changes without a supported objective.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: New, disputed or externally imposed change objectives, including urgent corrections.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: An informal exchange can leave competing interpretations or missing participants undiscoverable later; retain an explicit decision when that uncertainty matters.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Compare change with continued useful operation and retirement. End a classification or approval artefact when no consumer uses its distinction, while preserving any actual authorisation requirement.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Identify who may accept and deploy which changes, what evidence they need and when an automatic path must defer or stop. Failure: A generated conclusion can be mistaken for permission to mutate a repository or release a service.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Authorised maintainers or policy holders accept changes; generators cannot enlarge their own mandate from a successful test.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: Legitimate authority, actual action capability and explicit bounds for any delegation.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: A sole authorised maintainer may generate, inspect and accept a small change without separate roles; logical distinctions do not require separate people.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: Automated or delegated changes can alter shared artefacts or external behaviour.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Combining logical roles loses interpersonal challenge; it can be adequate for bounded tasks when independent evidence and explicit authority remain effective.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Existing legitimate decision authority remains; removal of ceremony does not permit unauthorised changes.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: A direct authorised maintainer decision can suffice for a bounded change.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: Actual access to required artefacts, dependency versions and restoration permissions; secrets need references or controlled recovery, not public copying.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: A lighter baseline may omit a mutable build input, schema or remote state; include any omitted input capable of changing the relevant result.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Identify build inputs and expected outputs; reproduce the relevant artefact or explain environmental variance and validate what is actually shipped. Failure: A patch validated in one environment may produce a different shipped artefact or be impossible to rebuild.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Build and release maintainers provide provenance; reproducibility does not grant trust in source correctness.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: Controlled or recorded toolchain/dependencies, available inputs and a declared comparison boundary.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: For a disposable local script, a versioned command and environment record may suffice; bit-for-bit output is not always the necessary observer.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Maintainer making the next decision

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITIONS: Stop expansion when remaining unknowns cannot alter the bounded decision; retire stale unconsumed views.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Identify the questions needed for this change, seek evidence until consequential uncertainties are bounded, and expand inquiry when evidence contradicts the model. Failure: Maintainers may either act without relevant understanding or spend disproportionate effort modelling irrelevant parts.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: The maintainer frames and tests explanations; affected experts can correct them but do not automatically authorise a patch.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: A change depends on unfamiliar behaviour, ownership, dependencies or intent.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Bounded inquiry can miss a question that would change the intervention; retain an explicit trigger for expanding inquiry when observations disagree.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Stop inquiry when the consequential question is adequately supported at acceptable risk; expand on contrary evidence. Retain only explanations with plausible future consumers.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Compare structural dependencies with representative execution, configuration and build evidence; investigate consequential disagreement. Failure: Either source structure or a small execution trace can be mistaken for the full behaviour of a configurable system.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Maintainers and operators supply complementary evidence; tool outputs are observations rather than approval.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: Known analysis scope and representative execution conditions; trace absence must not be read as impossibility.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Use one adequate analysis for a demonstrably closed local case; combining tools is not mandatory when it adds no discriminating observation.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: Dynamic binding, generated code, reflection, configuration or sparse tests make one evidence mode incomplete.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: A single evidence mode can miss its blind spots; the cheap path requires an adequately closed question, not mere agreement with the preferred explanation.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Stop inquiry when the consequential question is adequately supported at acceptable risk; expand on contrary evidence. Retain only explanations with plausible future consumers.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.ADOPTION_BOUNDARY: For a rejected, duplicate, ritual-only or unresolved candidate, this record is an adjudication/omission record, not an instruction to implement it.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Compute or inspect a slice relative to a declared criterion and analysis assumptions; treat it as evidence about that criterion, not the complete impact set. Failure: Unrelated code obscures the computations relevant to an observed value or proposed change.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Analysts choose the criterion; maintainers decide whether its omissions are acceptable for the actual change.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: Soundness assumptions for the chosen static/dynamic analysis, aliasing, control flow, termination and environment.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Direct inspection of a tiny dependency chain may be cheaper; avoid slicing where external effects are outside the model.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: A value, statement or behaviour can be represented by a tractable slicing criterion.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.COSTS_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Direct inspection loses systematic reach through complex dependencies; use a sound applicable analysis when manual omission risk becomes consequential.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Stop inquiry when the consequential question is adequately supported at acceptable risk; expand on contrary evidence. Retain only explanations with plausible future consumers.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PROTECTED_PROPERTY_AND_FAILURE: Label whether an activity recovers information, changes representation at the same abstraction, or reconstructs/changes the system; assign evidence and authority accordingly. Failure: Producing an explanation can be misreported as changing the system, or a transformation as merely documenting it.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.CONSUMER: Analysts recover evidence; authorised maintainers perform transformations; consumers must not infer one from the other.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.PREREQUISITES: Identification of input/output artefacts, abstraction level and whether external behaviour is intended to change.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Ordinary descriptions suffice for unambiguous local work; a taxonomy table is unnecessary.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NAME: Smallest coherent local maintenance
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.GUARD: A bounded change, a competent authorised maintainer, understood consumers and no complex state transition.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OPERATION: One person may clarify intent, inspect the relevant diff, run an adequate check and release with a feasible recovery/forward-repair condition. A read-only/pure local change can make data-recovery machinery inapplicable.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSIONS: No mandatory taxonomy form, board, slicing tool, metric dashboard, mutation campaign or separate actor per function.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.RETIREMENT: Remove temporary probes and notes with no continuing consumer; retain actual obligations and identity evidence needed later.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NAME: Continuous shared evolution
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.GUARD: Concurrent changes and independent consumers make integration feedback consequential.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NAME: Incremental displacement

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NAME: Quiescent cutover
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.GUARD: Accepted interruption and a credible stable write boundary exist; prolonged coexistence is disproportionately costly.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NAME: Bounded automation-assisted maintenance
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.GUARD: A supported task class has credible oracles, justified cost and explicit delegation.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OPERATION: Generator proposes, validators establish scoped evidence, authorised acceptance changes the real system and results are observed.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.OMISSIONS: A separate human approval step is not universally imposed for every narrow transformation; authority and independent evidence cannot be omitted.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.NAME: Stable service and deliberate non-change
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.GUARD: Current obligations and sustainable support are adequate; proposed intervention has no supported net benefit.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.RETIREMENT: End observations or support arrangements only as obligations disappear; switch to maintenance or retirement when conditions change.
FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.LIMIT: Inactivity alone does not establish the guard.

FROZEN_ORIGINAL_RECORD.GUARD: Continued operation is no longer justified or sustainable and remaining obligations can be resolved.
